explanation: Fires on the first numeral of an amount phrase that states how much or how many of something (counts, percentages, prices, measurements, multiples), peaking on that number word or digit (and on a thousands comma after it); it is strongest when a quantity modifier comes just before (about, around, nearly, approximately, roughly, over, more/less than, by) and weak (<1) when the numeral follows a determiner (the, these) or is a label such as 'Chapter 4' or a year. A minor offshoot fires on 'not'/'n't' after a do-auxiliary (does not, don't).
